A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MARSHAL and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. All 28 pages in each version support comparison, including relocated appendix material.

before.justification: V2 reports original game evaluations, downstream reasoning results, ablations, and failure analyses, including additional experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix experiments with Qwen3-8B, SPIRAL variants, and MT-GRPO.

M1.justification: The self-play procedure, turn-level return estimator, agent-specific normalization, objectives, and reward components remain unchanged. Section 3.2 revises their rationale without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three training games, three held-out games, and seven downstream reasoning benchmarks under single-agent, MAD, and AutoGen settings. Appendix coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Qwen baselines, SPIRAL, RAE variants, MT-GRPO, and MCTS/NE opponents. Renumbered appendix tables introduce no comparator additions or removals.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets, model sizes, game-evaluation counts, metrics, and generation limits are unchanged. V3 explicitly describes downstream evaluation as zero-shot but does not establish a changed procedure or rerun.

E4.justification: Both retain the fixed-opponent and advantage-component ablations, reasoning examples, failure analysis, algorithm-versus-game controls, and length-penalty sensitivity study. Their evidence is unchanged despite appendix relocation.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged. V3 adds no seed or independent-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 corrects the GPQA-Diamond gain from 6.57 to 7.57 percentage points; the abstract and introduction change 6.6 to 7.6. Tables 1 and 17 retain 37.88 for Qwen3-4B and 45.45 for the MARSHAL generalist under MAD, supporting the correction. Underlying result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the explicit mathematical assertion that summing normalized rewards generally produces non-zero-mean advantages. It substitutes a distribution-heterogeneity argument while retaining the equations, GAE-equivalence statement, and appendix theoretical comparison.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly qualify downstream gains as zero-shot and correct the headline GPQA improvement to 7.6. The central contributions and claims about generalizable multi-agent reasoning remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 changes the instability explanation from non-centered advantages to heterogeneous intermediate-reward distributions. Section 3.3 drops the claim about avoiding competitive-only overfitting, and the discussion specifies generalization to standard reasoning tasks. The two-player limitation remains.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 newly make the zero-shot evaluation description explicit. Software, hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged; moving the hyperparameter table adds no settings.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 softens positioning by removing its explicit criticism of prior competitive-only training as inducing overfitting. The cited-work set and main related-work comparisons remain unchanged; the revised Xu et al. bibliography entry identifies the same work.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, adds acknowledgments, updates affiliations and publication headers, and moves Hyperparameters from Appendix H to C. The main narrative and section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds colored emphasis to reasoning excerpts in Table 2, adjusts prompt-listing typography, and relocates the hyperparameter table from Table 13 to Table 5, reflowing subsequent appendix tables. Figures and result-table content are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 fixes a prominent numerical inconsistency: the retained GPQA scores differ by 7.57 points, agreeing with the revised claim. Explicit zero-shot wording, editorial corrections, and earlier hyperparameter placement also improve clarity. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the revised normalization rationale adds no proof, so the overall gain is limited.
